Cowan then expanded it into a transport and logistics group before selling the company to Schneider National in 2024.

long_biography.plain_text:
A chance to play for the Baltimore Colts gave Joseph W. Cowan an early alternative to the family trucking business. He instead joined the carrier founded by his father, ran its public warehouse operation and created a small irregular-route truckload service inside it. Years of competing with larger carriers shaped his preference for markets where scale was less decisive.

Cowan developed that operation into Cowan Systems around dedicated regional freight. He combined company-owned equipment with brokerage and intermodal services, then standardised lightweight tractors and trailers to carry heavier beverage loads. The regional model also gave drivers more predictable time at home, a practical response to the strains of long-haul work.
